the number of muscle fiber and its growth rate contribute to intralittter variation in postnatal performance and muscle characteristics, and the growth rate is the main contributor to intralittler variation in muscle fiber size.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the growth rate of the individual muscle fibers is a more important factor for growth rate differences between pigs within a litter, whereas the number and size of the individual muscle cells contribute more to the differences in growth rate between litters.
the intralitter differences in growth performance and muscle characteristics are due to a higher number of equal-sized muscle fiber in the fastest growing pigs.
the number of muscle cells and the growth rate per muscle cell are both important for the variation in postnatal muscle growth rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
muscle growth rate is not only determined by muscle fiber number but also by the size of the muscle fibers.

the number and growth rate of muscle cells are important factors in determining postnatal growth performance and that muscle fiber characteristics may be used as a tool in selection for postnatal growth rate.

within-litter variation in post-weaning growth rate is associated with a variation in muscle fiber growth characteristics, but that these differences are not associated with differences in meat quality.
